$schema_notes: Canonical, machine-readable Rakshak backend API contract for Citizen Web, Police Web, and Central Command Dashboard frontend teams. Generated from a live read-only audit of account 468704514492 (ap-south-1) on 2026-09-18, cross-checked against backend/lambdas/*/lambda_function.py source and docs/api-samples/*.json real captured payloads.
protocol: HTTP API (API Gateway v2), AWS_PROXY integration, payload format v2.0
auth: none -- every route is public. See SECURITY_MODEL.md.

route_counts.reconciliation_note: API_REFERENCE.md's prose states '14 frozen + 23 legacy = 37'; the actual deploy/routes.py source declares 15 contract + 20 legacy = 35. The remaining 2 live routes (OPTIONS /{proxy+}, POST /score/refresh) are undeclared -- see undocumented_live_routes. Recorded as an integration mismatch, not corrected in the existing prose docs by this audit (read-only scope).

routes.notes: INTEGRATION MISMATCH found during this audit: this route is absent from deploy/routes.py, AWS_RESOURCES.md, and API_REFERENCE.md, yet is live and callable -- confirmed by a real invocation 2026-09-18 (see FRONTEND_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md summary). status_codes.400: Bad request -- missing/invalid field, out-of-Chennai coordinate, invalid status transition, invalid status value
status_codes.404: Not found -- unknown sos_id/patrol_id/incident_id, or an unserviced pincode
status_codes.500: Unhandled error -- every handler wraps its router in try/except and returns {"error": str(e)}, never a raw Lambda crash trace
status_codes._note: These are the ONLY codes any Lambda handler emits (verified against every lambda_function.py in backend/lambdas/). 409/429/502/503/504 can only originate from API Gateway/Lambda infrastructure itself (throttling, timeout, cold-start failure), never from application code -- see ERROR_HANDLING_GUIDE.md.

known_field_inconsistencies: Prediction routes (GET /prediction/{zone}, POST /predict, GET /prediction/zone/{zoneId}) return camelCase safetyScore/riskLevel; heatmap/snapshot routes return snake_case safety_score/risk_level. Both are intentional, source-confirmed, and permanent -- see rakshak-dashboard/lambda_function.py _prediction() vs _zone_scores().
Incidents carry BOTH lat/lng and latitude/longitude (same values, dual spelling) -- citizen app and dashboard historically used different ones. Read either; prefer latitude/longitude in new code.

zone_name on an incident/patrol is sometimes just the raw pincode string (e.g. patrol P008's zone_name is '600023', not a real area name) when the pincode isn't in rakshak_common.ZONE_NAMES. Frontends must fall back to a local pincode->name map, same as dashboard/src/hooks/useActiveIncidents.js's PINCODE_NAME table.

Timeline/incident event objects are {type, ts, detail, patrol_id?, pincode?} -- DATABASE_SCHEMA.md's prose describes {type, message, timestamp, patrol_id} which does not match the live shape or the make_event() source. Use ts/detail.

PATCH .../status, .../resolve, and POST /sos/dispatch/{id} all return a PARTIAL object (sos_id, status, assigned_patrol_id[, eta_seconds]), never the full incident. Frontends must refetch GET /incident/{id} after any mutation to refresh events[]/patrol_position/etc.

distance_m only appears on a patrol view when status is Responding (en route to a scene); it is absent/null otherwise. battery and network on an incident are caller-supplied optionals, frequently null.
POST /score/refresh (undocumented, orphaned) uses safe_score as a 0..1 fraction, unlike every other route's 0..100 safetyScore/safety_score. Do not consume this route.
